articles.title: Philadelphia Phillies scary moment after foul ball nearly leaves trainer with a black eye
articles.standfirst: One foul ball nearly caused a serious injury in the Phillies' dugout.
articles.summary: One foul ball nearly caused a serious injury in the Phillies' dugout.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies defeated the Seattle Mariners 6-0 on Wednesday and continue their push to secure a spot in the postseason.

With the team in the middle of a playoff race, every member of the organization is crucial, including the medical staff. However, one of the trainers came dangerously close to suffering a serious injury during the game.

In the bottom of the third inning, Mariners catcher Jhonny Pereda hit a hard foul ball toward the Phillies’ dugout, where coaches and trainers were standing.

The ball struck one of the trainer’s sunglasses directly and completely shattered them. Fortunately, the lenses absorbed the impact and prevented the ball from hitting his eyes.

The trainer involved was Christian Bermúde z, a Phillies assistant trainer since 2021 . He joined the organization from Triple-A Lehigh Valley , where he worked as a medical operations liaison.

Philadelphia secured the three-game series against Seattle with a 2-1 record and will begin a new road trip on Friday against the Los Angeles Angels.

With the victory, the Phillies improved to 74-60 and remain four games behind the Atlanta Braves in the National League East . They are also just 2.5 games behind the Chicago Cubs in the National League Wild Card race.

The team managed to turn its season around after a difficult 9-19 start. Following the arrival of Don Mattingly as manager, Philadelphia gained momentum before the All-Star break, although the team has experienced ups and downs during the second half of the schedule.

Now, the Phillies are looking to pick up the pace down the stretch and secure their return to October baseball.

Last season, Philadelphia won the National League East division title, but their championship hopes ended after they were eliminated by the Los Angeles Dodgers in four games during the Division Series.

articles.title: Jesús Luzardo didn’t want to complicate Labor Day and made Phillies history
articles.standfirst: While thousands of fans enjoyed the holiday in Philadelphia, he decided to spend his afternoon in a much simpler way.
articles.summary: While thousands of fans enjoyed the holiday in Philadelphia, he decided to spend his afternoon in a much simpler way.
articles.body:
It was Labor Day, and Citizens Bank Park was packed as the Philadelphia Phillies faced the Atlanta Braves . More than 41,000 fans took advantage of the day off to enjoy some baseball, while both teams prepared for a game that, in principle, promised to be a long one. However, Jesús Luzardo seemed to have a different plan: not making things too complicated.

Atlanta managed just two hits, and Luzardo kept the opposing offense from finding a way to change the course of the game.

One run was all he needed

The problem for Philadelphia was that its own offense wasn’t finding much room either. The score remained 0-0 and, as the innings went by, every pitch from Luzardo made a small lead seem like it could be enough.

Then Kyle Schwarber appeared. In the bottom of the eighth inning, he hit a solo home run to break the tie and make it 1-0. One run . That was all Luzardo needed to try to finish the game himself.

He came back for the ninth inning with the crowd watching. Ha-Seong Kim hit a fly ball, but Ronald Acuña Jr. was hit by a pitch with two strikes, and suddenly the tying run was back on first base. Luzardo responded the way he had all afternoon: he struck out Drake Baldwin for his 12th strikeout and then got Ozzie Albies to fly out for the final out .

The first time he had done it in MLB

Luzardo finished all nine innings allowing just two hits, one walk and 12 strikeouts on 109 pitches, 78 of them for strikes . But the most important part was what he had just accomplished: the first shutout and complete game of his Major League career.

The performance also came in his 150th MLB start and allowed him to surpass 200 strikeouts for the season once again. His 2026 record improved to 14-5, while his ERA dropped to 2.87 .

For the Phillies, the 1-0 victory meant splitting the four-game series against Atlanta and gaining ground in the race for the National League East . For Luzardo, it was another demonstration of why he has become one of the most important arms in the rotation.

And while most people took advantage of Labor Day to rest, spend the afternoon at the ballpark and enjoy a day away from work, Jesús Luzardo found a pretty spectacular way to make sure his workday ended quickly .
